Their contributions are small and spread evenly, with no single dominant signal. A few rarer n-grams are somewhat more suggestive of numeric computation. DIV MUL (+0.007725, freq 0.000016) and CDQ MOV (+0.013155, freq 0.000101) point to arithmetic or sign-extension work, and MOV FLD (+0.008216, freq 0.000848) points to floating-point loads. Even so, these are low-frequency and non-specific, and no function names, API calls, or constants were supplied to confirm a mining workload. The model's strong output suggests this binary's instruction-sequence profile resembles known malicious samples in the training data. The evidence itself is circumstantial and does not independently establish cryptojacking, so the tier is low-confidence, not high-confidence.
